To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proton has a very small but non-zero radius of about 0.8 fm (2) the proton is a very complicated object made up of three quarks, which are bound to each other by gluons, and (3) the proton can be described as a three-quark object that is very similar to a bag of jelly.

the quark-gluon structure of the proton is not static but fluctuating, that the fluctuations are not random but correlated, that the correlations are not local in time and space but extend over large distances, and that the correlations are sensitive to the quantum state of the proton.

the proton spin is not carried by the quark spin, that the proton spin has an important contribution from the quarks’ orbital angular momentum, and that the quarks’ spin and orbital angular momenta are not independent of each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of protons and how they interact with other particles.
the study of the proton, the most fundamental particle in the visible universe.
the study of quarks, gluons and their interactions, and the strong nuclear force.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a proton consists of two up quarks, one down quark, and the gluons that bind them together.
a proton is a bound state of the three valence quarks (two up quarks and one down quark) with a sea of quark–antiquark pairs, and gluons.
protons and neutorns are made of up and down (and other) quarks. But what are quarks made of?
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the strong force is not strong at all.
we are trying to understand the strong interaction between quarks and gluons that make up protons.
we have found a way of measuring the quark content of the proton, the quark distribution, with unprecedented accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton is not a simple bag of three quarks, but rather a complex system of quarks, gluons and other particles.
there are no new particles in the proton, only new forces, and the forces are very weak.
there is a lot of structure in the proton that we have yet to understand.
